findings.title: Outbound webhook idempotency is non-atomic in the API and absent in the worker dispatcher
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:178-180 — per-endpoint key `${idempotencyBaseKey}:${endpoint.id}` claimed atomically via claimIdempotencyKey (Redis SET NX EX) before delivery
apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:182-186 — sends Idempotency-Key header and persists idempotency_key on the delivery row (line 219)
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:80-92 — worker dispatcher makes the same atomic per-endpoint claim and skips duplicates
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:98-100,124,179 — worker sends and persists the same Idempotency-Key
apps/api/src/lib/idempotency.ts:99-136 — claimIdempotencyKey is an atomic SET NX EX with in-memory mutex fallback
apps/api/src/__tests__/webhook-dispatcher-idempotency.test.ts:116-150 — 3 concurrent dispatches collapse to 1 fetch and 1 delivery row; claim released on failure
apps/worker/src/__tests__/webhook-dispatcher.test.ts:120-137 — duplicate worker job collapses to a single delivery
findings.impact: Duplicate outbound events can no longer double-deliver under concurrency; consumers also receive a stable Idempotency-Key for their own dedup.
findings.recommendation: Keep the atomic claim as the single idempotency authority; add a regression test that asserts the claim is per-endpoint (fan-out to N endpoints yields N deliveries, 1 per endpoint).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: both dispatchers claim atomically and carry Idempotency-Key; delivery rows store idempotency_key; tests cover concurrent-duplicate collapse — mainecybertech#129/d5e0d5b7 lineage now on main.

findings.title: M365 inbound notifications have no enforced timestamp/replay window
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:27 — M365_REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS = 7 days
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:622-632 — deterministic digest of the full notification is atomically claimed with the 7-day TTL (dedupWebhook(m365Key, M365_REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS))
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:29-51,641 — after processing, logWebhookDelivery calls storeIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey, "done")
apps/api/src/lib/idempotency.ts:50,138-164 — storeIdempotencyKey hardcodes IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS = 24h (redis SETEX / in-memory entry), overwriting the 7-day claim
apps/api/src/__tests__/webhooks.test.ts:592-613 — test asserts only the claim TTL (7d), not the post-processing store TTL, so the 24h reset is untested
findings.impact: The enforced M365 replay window is effectively 24 hours, not the documented 7 days: a captured/retransmitted notification (clientState included) is accepted again after 24h. Provider retries (~4h) are still covered, so the practical risk is a stale replay re-running audit/delivery logging, not state mutation.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the claim TTL when marking the key done — e.g. storeIdempotencyKey(key, "done", ttlSeconds) with the same M365 window (or use claimIdempotencyKey's value update), and extend the test to assert the final TTL after a successful M365 request.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the 7-day atomic claim on the notification digest exists (mainecybertech#122), but logWebhookDelivery:47 storeIdempotencyKey resets the same key to the 24h default (idempotency.ts:50,144), so the effective window is 24h — residual documented.

findings.impact: The inline fallback no longer misreports attempts and no longer conflicts with the worker retry task; delivery logs are truthful.
findings.recommendation: No action; keep the single-retry-owner rule when changing retry semantics.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: actual attempt count and dead_letter marking present, single retry owner enforced — mainecybertech#129 (68fd8d12) now on main.

findings.title: No per-provider payload schema or size cap on webhook ingress (global 10mb JSON limit)
evidence: apps/api/src/app.ts:110-120 — express.json({ limit: '10mb', type: [application/json, application/csp-report, application/reports+json] }) applies to every route, including /api/v1/webhooks/*
apps/api/src/app.ts:138-143 — rate limiter skips req.path.startsWith('/api/v1/webhooks/'), so the 10mb parse is unauthenticated and unthrottled
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:351-358,453-461,570-588 — inbound handlers consume req.body directly (optional chaining) with no Zod/JSON-schema validation; only signature/clientState gating
apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:37-51 — CRUD uses Zod, but inbound provider bodies do not
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:590-604,612-627 — M365 iterates the value array before dedup, so a large batch is parsed/iterated in full
findings.impact: Any unauthenticated client can force a 10mb JSON parse (memory/CPU amplification) on webhook routes; malformed provider payloads are accepted into logging/processing instead of a clean 400/413.
findings.recommendation: Mount a tighter per-route JSON limit for /api/v1/webhooks/* (e.g. 256kb-1mb) and add per-provider Zod schemas that reject unknown/oversized payloads before side effects; consider a modest IP rate limit on inbound webhook paths.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still one global 10mb parser, no inbound schema validation, and webhook routes remain rate-limit exempt. No migration/route change since 9c0b88c.

findings.title: Webhook raw body typed as `string` but consumed as `Buffer`
evidence: apps/api/src/app.ts:116-117 — verify hook declares req.rawBody?: string and assigns buf.toString() (bytes → UTF-8 string)
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:152-153 — Stripe constructEvent receives (req as { rawBody?: Buffer }).rawBody as Buffer, a type-level lie (runtime value is a string)
apps/api/src/lib/webhook-signature.ts:32-36 — rawBodyBuffer tolerates both string and Buffer, so the HMAC paths are safe
apps/api/src/__tests__/helpers.ts:86-88 — test app mirrors the same string assignment
findings.impact: Runtime behavior is correct (Stripe and rawBodyBuffer accept strings), but the mismatched type contract can hide a real bug if a future consumer assumes Buffer (e.g. byte-exact HMAC on non-UTF-8 input).
findings.recommendation: Store the raw bytes: req.rawBody = buf (Buffer), declare rawBody?: Buffer on the request type, and drop the `as Buffer` cast at webhooks.ts:153.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: app.ts:117 still stores a string and webhooks.ts:153 still casts it to Buffer.

findings.title: No alerting when webhook dead-letters accumulate or payment reconciliation drifts
evidence: infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml — alert groups are mct-service-availability, mct-admin-abuse and RLS-share rules; grep 'webhook' returns 0 matches
apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:136-145 — portal_webhook_dead_letters_total exists but is not referenced by any rule

apps/worker/src/main.ts:81-89 — webhook-retry runs every 5 minutes with no alert on its failures

findings.title: Admin dead-letter retry of inline-dispatched failures no-ops and deletes the DLQ row
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:208-220 — inline failures persist a PII-safe summary request_body {event, receivedAt} (no `data`) and dead_letter: true
apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:109-116 — the matching DLQ row also stores request_body {event, receivedAt}
apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:185-205 — POST /dead-letters/:id/retry recreates a due-now delivery from deadLetter.request_body and deletes the DLQ row
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:69-77 — rows whose request_body has no `data` are marked dead_letter: true and skipped WITHOUT re-inserting a DLQ row
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/webhooks/dead-letters/DeadLetterActions.tsx:20-23 — the UI reports success ('re-queued for delivery') on the route's ok response
findings.impact: For failures produced by the API inline fallback (queue/Redis unavailable), an operator's Retry removes the dead-letter record, attempts no HTTP delivery, and shows a success toast — silent loss of the failure record and a false success.
findings.recommendation: Make retry truthful: keep the DLQ row until the retry task reports an actual attempt, and have webhook-retry re-insert a DLQ row (with a reason) when it skips a no-data row; alternatively have the inline dispatcher persist the replayable payload (or mark such rows as non-replayable and disable Retry in the UI).
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: code-traced, no test covers the no-data retry branch (worker webhook-retry.test.ts:69-85 only covers empty/failed query).

findings.title: `webhook-retry` has no row claim: concurrent retry runs can double-send deliveries
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:16-30 — selects up to 20 failed rows (status failed, dead_letter false, retry_count < 5, due) with no claim/FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:47-220 — sends and then updates retry_count/next_retry_at; two overlapping runs both read and POST the same rows
apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:196 — admin retry enqueues 'webhook-retry' directly, bypassing the scheduler lock
apps/worker/src/main.ts:81-89 — scheduled every 5 minutes; apps/worker/src/lib/scan-lock.ts:26-73 only serializes the scheduled enqueue per replica
apps/worker/src/consumer-bullmq.ts:15,31 and apps/worker/src/env.ts:9 — BullMQ concurrency defaults to 10, so a scheduled and an admin-triggered job run concurrently
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:85-87 — retries preserve the Idempotency-Key header, which mitigates consumers that dedupe
findings.impact: Duplicate outbound deliveries and racy retry_count/dead-letter transitions under overlapping retry runs; consumers without idempotent handlers can double-process (e.g. duplicate ticket creation).
findings.recommendation: Claim each row atomically before sending (UPDATE ... SET next_retry_at = now() + lease WHERE id = ? AND retry_count = ? / SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), or claim the delivery idempotency key in the retry path; add a concurrency test with two overlapping webhookRetry calls.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: worker retry task has no claim/lock; webhook-retry.test.ts:69-85 does not exercise concurrency.

findings.title: Retried deliveries replay a body without the envelope `timestamp` (payload drift)
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:65 — original delivery body is {event, timestamp, data}
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:170 — the stored request_body is {event, data} (timestamp not persisted)
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:79 — retry body = JSON.stringify(delivery.request_body), so the retried payload omits timestamp
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:111-115 — a fresh HMAC is computed over the changed body, so signature verification passes but the payload differs from the first attempt
findings.impact: Consumers that validate the documented envelope (timestamp present/fresh) will reject or mis-handle retries; the retried payload is not byte-identical to the original delivery.
findings.recommendation: Persist the full original body (including timestamp) in request_body and replay it verbatim, or document that retries carry {event,data} only; add a test asserting the retry body equals the first-attempt body.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: request_body omits the envelope timestamp and retry replays the stored object as-is.

findings.title: Delivery inserts ignore unique-key conflicts, losing the successful-attempt record
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302053_webhook_idempotency.sql:12-23 — webhook_deliveries_idempotency_unique unique (idempotency_key)
apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:226-230 — the claim is deleted on failure so a later dispatch can reprocess the same key
apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:208-220 — the later dispatch inserts the same idempotency_key with no error check on the insert result
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:166-180 — same unchecked insert pattern
apps/api/src/__tests__/webhook-dispatcher-idempotency.test.ts:52-70 — the supabase mock always returns {error: null}, so conflicts are untestable today
findings.impact: After a failed delivery is re-dispatched successfully, the success row is rejected by the unique constraint and silently dropped: the admin delivery log keeps showing the failure while the endpoint's last_success_at says success.
findings.recommendation: Check the insert result and update/upsert the existing row on conflict (or log the conflict); add a test that a re-dispatch after failure records the successful attempt.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: code-traced conflict path; not reproduced against a live DB (mock returns no error).

findings.title: Outbound webhook response bodies are read without a size cap
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/pinned-fetch.ts:91-99 — accumulates every response chunk in memory (chunks.push) and concatenates without a maximum size
apps/worker/src/lib/pinned-fetch.ts (same implementation) — used by dispatcher and retry
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:158 and apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:477 — res.text() reads the entire response body
apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:172, apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:497 — the full body is stored in webhook_deliveries.response_body
findings.impact: A configured (or compromised) endpoint returning an unbounded body can exhaust API/worker memory; the 10s abort does not bound bytes received.
findings.recommendation: Cap the response read (e.g. 64kb) in pinnedFetch and truncate/omit response_body beyond the cap; add a test with an oversized response.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: no max-size guard in either pinned-fetch copy or at the call sites.

findings.title: M365 handler processes only the first notification in a batch (value[0])
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:583-588 — value array is accepted and required non-empty
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:590-604 — clientState is validated for every notification in the batch
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:612-613,627 — processing and the dedup digest use only value[0] (const notification = value[0])
apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:634-642 — audit/delivery logging and the metric cover only the first notification, while metadata records notificationCount: value.length
findings.impact: If Graph batches multiple change notifications into one request, all but the first are silently dropped from logging/audit and are not covered by the replay digest (a later batch containing the first notification again would be deduped while its new members are ignored).
findings.recommendation: Iterate all notifications (per-notification dedup key and audit/delivery record), or explicitly document and log that only value[0] is processed; add a multi-notification batch test.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: code-evident value[0] handling; provider batching behavior not reproduced from the repo.

findings.title: No retention/cleanup for webhook_deliveries and webhook_dead_letters
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:123-135 — the retention task purges only audit_logs and notifications
grep 'webhook' apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts — no webhook table appears in the purge config
supabase/migrations/5302032_webhook_endpoints.sql:47-61 and 5302050_webhook_retry_dlq.sql:11-23 — delivery/DLQ rows have created_at but no TTL/cleanup job
apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:75-134 — DLQ rows accumulate with no bulk-archive/export path
findings.impact: Delivery history and dead letters grow without bound; stale DLQ rows (including the non-replayable inline rows above) are never cleared, increasing storage and operator noise.
findings.recommendation: Add webhook_deliveries/webhook_dead_letters to the retention task with documented windows (e.g. 90d deliveries, 180d DLQ) and bounded batch deletes; alert on DLQ depth first.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: retention task covers audit_logs/notifications only.

## Executive Summary

The webhook surface is materially stronger than the previous full run. Both outbound dispatchers now claim a per-endpoint idempotency key atomically (Redis `SET NX EX`), send it as `Idempotency-Key`, and persist it on the delivery row; inbound Jira/JSM signatures fail closed unless the captured raw body exists; M365 uses a constant-time `clientState` gate with a 7-day replay claim; outbound delivery is SSRF-pinned on all four paths; DLQ/delivery counters exist; and the admin UI/API exposes dead letters with retry/dismiss and audit logging. The previous WH-P1 findings and four of the WH-P2 findings are verified fixed on main.

Remaining risks are concentrated in the retry/DLQ lifecycle and hardening edges:

1. The M365 "7-day" replay window is effectively 24 hours because the post-processing `storeIdempotencyKey` resets the TTL (WH-P2-001 residual).
2. The admin dead-letter Retry action silently discards inline-dispatched dead letters without attempting delivery (new P2).
3. `webhook-retry` has no row claim, so overlapping runs can double-send (new P2).
4. Inbound webhook routes still share the global 10mb JSON parser, have no per-provider schema, and are exempt from rate limiting (WH-P2-006).
5. `webhook_dead_letters` still has no DELETE policy, and reads are not gated by the existing `webhooks:view` permission; per-endpoint signing secrets remain plaintext with no rotation.

Recommended next actions: fix the TTL reset, make DLQ retry truthful, claim retry rows, add per-route body limits + schemas, add the DLQ DELETE policy and read permission, and add a DLQ alert rule.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Inbound receivers and signature verification

- Evidence: `webhooks.ts:131-653`; `webhook-signature.ts:3-73`; `app.ts:110-120`.
- What it does: Stripe uses `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent` over `req.rawBody`; Jira/JSM require `x-hub-signature` and the captured raw body and reject 401 when it is missing, then enforce a 5-minute timestamp window with `requireTimestamp: true`; M365 authenticates every notification by constant-time `clientState` and fails closed (501 unset / 401 mismatch).
- Current controls: HMAC-SHA256 timing-safe compare; per-event dedup keys (`stripe-<id>`, body-hash Jira/JSM keys, M365 notification digest); audit + delivery logging; claim released on handler failure so provider retries reprocess.
- Missing controls: per-provider schemas, per-route body cap, inbound rate limiting; M365 processes only `value[0]`; the M365 replay claim TTL is reset to 24h after processing.
- Risks: WH-P2-001 residual, WH-P2-006, M365 batch handling.
- Suggested tests: oversized body → 413; malformed provider payload → 400; multi-notification M365 batch; final TTL assertion after processing.

### Item: Outbound dispatchers (API inline + worker queue)

- Evidence: `lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:134-262`; `worker/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:36-219`; `lib/task-producer.ts:76-105`.
- What it does: The API prefers the queue; the inline fallback fans out per endpoint with an atomic per-endpoint claim, HMAC signing, 3 attempts (200ms/400ms backoff), truthful `retry_count`, dead-letter on failure and release of the claim; the worker does the same with a 10s timeout, pinned fetch, blocked-URL dead-lettering and `next_retry_at` scheduling.
- Current controls: Idempotency-Key header + persisted key; DB unique constraint; org-scoped endpoint lookup; PII-safe summaries on the inline path (full payload on the worker path).
- Missing controls: retry-task row claim; conflict handling on delivery inserts; bounded response reads.
- Risks: new findings on retry concurrency, payload drift, silent insert conflicts, unbounded response bodies.

### Item: Worker retry + dead-letter lifecycle

- Evidence: `worker/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:12-230`; `worker/main.ts:81-89`; `lib/scan-lock.ts:26-73`; `routes/webhook-management.ts:75-258`.
- What it does: Every 5 minutes (one replica via scan lock) the task selects up to 20 due failed rows, retries with the preserved Idempotency-Key and re-signed HMAC, updates `retry_count`/`next_retry_at` with 1m×2^n backoff, and dead-letters after 5 attempts. Admins can list/retry/dismiss DLQ rows; retry recreates a due-now delivery and deletes the DLQ row.
- Current controls: SSRF guard + pinned fetch; attempt counting; audit events; UI confirm dialog for dismiss.
- Missing controls: row claim/lock; truthful retry for non-replayable rows; DLQ DELETE policy; retention; alerting.
- Risks: the retry no-op (P2), concurrent double-send (P2), WH-P2-005, IR-P2-003.

### Item: Secrets and admin management

- Evidence: `5302032:8`; `webhook-management.ts:20-51,168-397,430-542`; `env.ts:54-59`; `SECRETS_ROTATION.md:52-54`.
- What it does: Endpoint secrets are masked on GET, audit metadata keys containing "secret" are redacted (`services/audit.ts:34-45`), provider secrets are deploy-wired and in the rotation inventory, and CRUD mutations require `webhooks:manage` with optimistic locking and audit logs.
- Missing controls: GET routes are not permission-gated; endpoint secrets have no expiry/rotation metadata and are absent from the rotation doc; POST/PATCH responses return the secret unmasked to the caller.
- Risks: ACM-P2-005, ACM-P2-007.

## Findings

23 findings (2 P1, 12 P2, 9 P3; statuses: 7 verified-fixed, 2 partially-fixed, 7 still-open, 7 open). Titles below; full evidence/impact/recommendation in the JSON.

**Verified fixed (this run):** Outbound webhook idempotency is non-atomic in the API and absent in the worker dispatcher; M365 webhook auth depends on `M365_CLIENT_STATE`…; Inline dispatcher records a fixed `retry_count`…; Outbound and DLQ delivery outcomes are not metered…; Inbound Jira/JSM signature falls back to re-serialized JSON…; Worker queued webhook dispatcher inserts deliveries without an idempotency key; Webhook SSRF guard has a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU window.

**Partially fixed:** M365 inbound notifications have no enforced timestamp/replay window (7-day claim reset to 24h); No committed event catalog or webhook documentation for consumers (module docs exist; no catalog; stale M365 claims).

**Still open:** `webhook_dead_letters` has no DELETE policy…; No per-provider payload schema or size cap…; Test endpoint generates a random idempotency key…; Webhook raw body typed as `string` but consumed as `Buffer`; Webhook endpoint and delivery reads are available to any org member…; Webhook signing secrets are stored plaintext with no rotation or expiry; No alerting when webhook dead-letters accumulate… (webhook half).

**New:** Admin dead-letter retry of inline-dispatched failures no-ops and deletes the DLQ row (P2); `webhook-retry` has no row claim: concurrent retry runs can double-send deliveries (P2); Retried deliveries replay a body without the envelope `timestamp` (P3); Delivery inserts ignore unique-key conflicts… (P3); Outbound webhook response bodies are read without a size cap (P3); M365 handler processes only the first notification in a batch (P3); No retention/cleanup for `webhook_deliveries` and `webhook_dead_letters` (P3).

## Recommendations

### Immediate / Release Blocking

1. Fix the M365 replay TTL reset (`storeIdempotencyKey` must not shorten the 7-day claim) and add a test asserting the post-processing TTL.
2. Make DLQ retry truthful: do not delete the DLQ row until a delivery attempt happens; re-insert a DLQ row when the retry task skips a non-replayable row, or disable Retry for those rows in the UI.

### This Week

3. Add a row claim/lease to `webhook-retry` (or `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`) and a concurrency test.
4. Add a tighter per-route JSON limit for `/api/v1/webhooks/*` plus per-provider Zod schemas.
5. Add the `webhook_dead_letters` DELETE policy and gate webhook read routes with `requirePermission('webhooks','view')`.
6. Add a Prometheus rule on `portal_webhook_dead_letters_total` growth and the outbound failure ratio.

### This Month

7. Persist/replay the full outbound body (including `timestamp`) on retries.
8. Handle unique-key conflicts on delivery inserts (update/upsert or log).
9. Document outbound endpoint secret rotation and add `last_rotated_at`/expiry guidance.
10. Publish the event catalog and correct the M365 statements in `docs/modules/webhooks.md`.

### Later / Platform Evolution

11. Cap outbound response reads and truncate stored `response_body`.
12. Process all M365 notifications in a batch (or explicitly document value[0]).
13. Add retention/cleanup for `webhook_deliveries`/`webhook_dead_letters`.
14. Consider making Redis mandatory for webhook dedup (fail closed vs per-process fallback) and adding jitter to retry backoff.

## Suggested Tests

- Unit: `storeIdempotencyKey` preserves a caller-provided TTL (M365 7d) and does not shorten it.
- Unit/route: DLQ retry on a no-`data` dead letter leaves the DLQ row intact and returns a non-success or "non-replayable" state.
- Worker: `webhookRetry` concurrency — two overlapping invocations against the same due row must produce one HTTP attempt (row claim).
- Worker: retry body fidelity — the retried body equals the first-attempt body (including `timestamp`) and the HMAC verifies.
- API: re-dispatch after a failed delivery records the successful attempt despite the unique idempotency key.
- API: inbound >limit body → 413; malformed Jira/JSM/Stripe/M365 payload → 400 before side effects.
- API: GET webhook routes → 403 for an org member without `webhooks:view`; 200 for a member with it.
- RLS: non-super-admin org admin deletes a DLQ row under the user-scoped client and one row is removed.
- Security: hostname re-resolving to a private IP between guard and connect is still blocked (pinned fetch).
- E2E: admin retry/dismiss flows show accurate success/failure states (extend `apps/web/e2e/admin/webhooks.spec.ts`).
- CI/ops: `promtool test rules` for the new DLQ alert thresholds.
